# oauth/v1

An OAuth 2.1 authorization server for the app: authorization code with PKCE, device code, refresh, revocation, and
client registration (dynamic, or by a client metadata document). The CLI's browser login and MCP clients such as
Claude sign in through it, and get API tokens ([api-tokens/v1](/docs/contracts/api-tokens/v1)).

A routed contract ([oauth.go](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/oauth/v1/oauth.go)): the OAuth specs fix its API's shape, so its provider serves it as it is.

## Use

| HTTP | What it does |
|---|---|
| `GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` | the server's metadata (RFC 8414 puts it at the root) |
| `GET` / `POST /api/_c/oauth/v1/authorize` | sign in and consent (browser) |
| `POST /api/_c/oauth/v1/token` | codes and refresh tokens for access tokens |
| `POST /api/_c/oauth/v1/device` | start a device-code sign-in |
| `GET` / `POST /api/_c/oauth/v1/device/verify` | enter the device code (browser) |
| `POST /api/_c/oauth/v1/revoke` | revoke a token |
| `POST /api/_c/oauth/v1/register` | dynamic client registration (when on) |
| `GET` / `POST /api/_c/oauth/v1/provider/callback` | sign-in through an OAuth2 provider (Google, Apple, ...) |

In Go, another extension (MCP) turns on dynamic registration and sets token lifetimes:
`oauthv1.Contract.Of(app)` → `EnableDynamicRegistration()`, `SetAccessTTL(path, ttl)`, `Issuer(e)`.

## Provide

Implement `oauthv1.Server` and serve the routes above (`extkit.EventServer` or `extkit.RouteBinder`); issue access
tokens through api-tokens/v1.

## Commands and APIs

Its own HTTP API under `/api/_c/oauth/v1/`, described above. It has no generated commands or MCP tools. [Remote CLI](/docs/features/remote) explains how PocketOne apps are managed from afar.
